Third-Party and Integration Security Policy
   Document no.                 TPS-POL-02

   Version                      2.1

   Effective                    01 January 2025

   Policy owner                 Chief Information Security Officer (position vacant since September 2025; IT Security
                                Administrator acting)

   Applies to                   All third-party integrations with access to financial or customer data


 1. Risk classification
 Any vendor with write access to a financial system, or read access to customer data, is classified HIGH risk.

 2. Integration credential requirements
 2.1 Integration credentials must be restricted to the vendor's published IP addresses wherever the platform
 supports it.
 2.2 Integration credentials must expire within 90 days and be rotated on expiry.
 2.3 Credentials must carry only the minimum scope needed. 'All modules' or 'admin' scope requires a documented
 justification.

 3. Vendor review
 3.1 HIGH risk vendors must be reviewed at least every 12 months, including a check that vendor assurance covers
 the systems that hold or protect Harbor & Finch credentials.

 4. Monitoring
 4.1 Alerts must be configured for bulk exports and for deletion of export jobs by integration accounts on systems
 holding financial or customer data.

 5. Handling credentials in support work
 5.1 Staff must not ask customers or partners to paste credentials or keys into tickets or chat. A secure
 credential-submission link must be used.
 5.2 Any credential found in a ticket must be reported to IT Security and rotated.

 6. Exceptions
 6.1 Exceptions require written approval of the CISO and may last no longer than six months.

 7. Transition
 7.1 Integrations created before 01 January 2025 must meet sections 2 and 4 by 01 January 2026.

 Version history
   Version        Date                       Change

   2.0            03 Aug 2023                Initial policy

   2.1            01 Jan 2025                Added sections 2.2, 4.1, 5 and 7 following board review

 Dear Customer,
 Our monitoring identified unusual activity affecting a limited subset of customer connections to TallyBridge

 There is no evidence that customer data was accessed in a way that affects business operations. No action is

 Please do not forward this notice outside your organisation.

Email: Update from TallyBridge Software
   From                  security-notices@tallybridge.example

   To                    accounts@harborfinch.example; it-security@harborfinch.example

   Date                  Fri, 28 Aug 2026, 18:10 IST

   Subject               Update: investigation findings and next steps

 Dear Customer,
 We have completed our investigation of the activity reported in our notice of 21 August. Our findings are
 summarised below.

 What we found
 1. Unauthorised requests were made using a customer connection credential on 11 and 12 August 2026 only.
 2. The access was limited to support ticket metadata. We have found no evidence that finance records or stored
 files were accessed.
 3. All temporary export files created during the activity have been removed.
 4. The activity originated entirely from outside our network. No systems inside our environment or on the
 private link were involved.

 What we did
 5. Affected credentials were rotated on 24 August 2026.
 6. A list of indicators is attached to assist your review (file: indicator_list.csv).

 What is changing
 7. From 1 September 2026, TallyBridge Connect will also synchronise vendor contact details (email and phone)
 between your systems, using the existing connection. No action is needed.
 We consider this matter closed. Thank you for your patience.
 Regards,
 Customer Trust Team, TallyBridge Software

 Please do not forward this notice outside your organisation.
